_comment: HAND-DERIVED AS3 semantics for every case in NullCases.as. Never regenerate this file by running either arm: the point of the probe is that the rule and AIR agree independently.
_derivation: The AS3 conditional operator `cond ? a : b` returns a when cond is true and b when cond is false (AS3 language reference, conditional operator). Each case's condition therefore picks the branch: 6 tests `x != null` with a live object (TRUE -> the THEN branch `Bitmap(x)`); 2 tests `x == null` (FALSE -> the ELSE branch, which is the null literal, so the value IS null -- the first cut of this table said "ok" here and the AIR arm caught the mistake, which is precisely why the reference is checked and not assumed); every other case tests `x == null` with a live object (FALSE) or a constant false (case 3), so it must evaluate the ELSE branch, whose value is a live object -- that is the whole point. Nothing about the TYPE of the result may change which branch runs, and a null literal in the THEN slot is just a value.
_derivation_extended: Cases 15-17 ask whether the collapse is specific to reference results. 12 is NOT one of them: its THEN branch is the literal 0, not null, so both branches are int and no null is involved (it is the control for `the same shape without a null literal`). 15/16/17 put the null literal in the THEN slot with a Number/Boolean/int result; the condition is false with a live x, so the value must be 42 / true / 7. If our AOT answers 0 / false / 0 instead, the collapse silently zeroes scalar results too -- a quieter failure than the NULL case, and one an all-object table would have missed.

label.1: x == null ? null : Bitmap(x)      [the reported shape]
label.2: x == null ? Bitmap(x) : null      [cond FALSE -> else IS the null]
label.4: x == null ? null : x              [x:Object, no cast]
label.5: x == null ? null : x              [x:Bitmap, no cast]
label.6: x != null ? Bitmap(x) : null      [the workaround shape]
label.9: x == null ? null : bm.bitmapData   [another class type]
label.10: o == null ? null : Bitmap(o)       [o out of a {} slot]
label.11: x == null ? null : String('hi')    [value type: control]
label.12: x == null ? 0 : 42                  [then is 0, NOT the null literal: control]
label.13: if (x == null) return null; return Bitmap(x)  [workaround]
label.14: x == null ? null : wrap(x)         [call in ELSE]
